The mucosa of the upper larynx (above the vocal folds) is innervated by the internal laryngeal nerve (a branch of the superior laryngeal nerve). This nerve carries sensory information from the laryngeal mucosa and serves as the afferent limb of the cough reflex. The gag reflex, in contrast, has its afferent limb in the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX).

ANSWER: E
